items.title: ytunnel
items.author: Curator
items.content:
ytunnel is a CLI and a TUI for managing Cloudflare Tunnels under your own domains.

It creates tunnels and DNS records, then starts or stops local cloudflared processes. The dashboard places tunnel status beside logs and request metrics, and supports switching between Cloudflare accounts.

Managed tunnels run through launchd on macOS or systemd on Linux and continue after the dashboard closes. Temporary tunnels clean up after a normal exit. Tunnels created outside ytunnel are listed read-only and the setup requires cloudflared, an API token and a domain managed by Cloudflare.

For developers and system administrators already using Cloudflare DNS, ytunnel works best for those sharing local services and maintaining persistent access to them.

items.title: gnat
items.author: Curator
items.content:
gnat is a keyboard-driven TUI client for managing NATS service and JetStream streams, consumers and stored data.

It features a dashboard displaying all the connection information to the chosen NATS server including the messages throughput, per-stream messages and the message details. Generally, it can create, modify and delete streams collected in the dashboard, and edits entries in key-value buckets. Saved connection profiles support authentication and TLS settings in gnat.

Additionally, gnat allows for searching messages and their contents in the dashboard. It supports JSON payloads or JSONPath filtering as you search for messages and it shows these results in the monitor stream. In the consumer views, it can preview message counts and their delivery state, with a separate dashboard for monitoring them.

For developers and system administrators and network specialists running NATS, gnat is practical for investigating message delivery and maintaining JetStream resources from a minimal terminal interface.

items.title: llm-visuals
items.author: Curator
items.content:
llm-visuals is a terminal dashboard for monitoring active local LLM inference and GPU performance.

It detects running inference servers, including ollama, and displays prefill and decoding speed measured in tokens per second, and time to first token with context usage and GPU memory and load statistics. The performance view combines throughput histories and it has the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) balance view showing the GPU load of each expert in active inference.

One other useful view in llm-visuals is the bandwidth section that indicates which part of the hardware pipeline is bottlenecked or actively decode / or prefill bound. The active experts can be visualized in 3D to give the perspective of the current GPU inference activity. 

For machine learning engineers, researchers, inference engineers and software engineers that running local models, llm-visuals is useful to help with investigating inference slowdowns and watching how requests use available hardware.

items.title: terrascope
items.author: Curator
items.content:
terrascope is an interactive terminal world map with weather, aircraft and earthquake layers all visible inside of your terminal.

It draws country outlines and place labels using braille cells with keyboard and mouse controls for panning, zooming and selecting markers. Separate tabs show forecasts, aircraft positions and trails, or day/night bands with timezone information.

This tool fetches detailed map data into a local cache and reuses it on later runs. It is possible to use it offline to disable live requests and it can use the cache data for optimal performance and fresh weather and aircraft positions depend on the availability of external providers used in terrascope.

For those who enjoy exploring maps, weather and lots of geological information, terrascope suits those exploring geography alongside changing weather and flight activity in the terminal.

items.title: ipatool
items.author: Curator
items.content:
ipatool is a CLI for searching the App Store and downloading Apple app packages.

It downloads apps by bundle identifier or numeric ID, producing .ipa files or macOS .pkg packages. Depending on the Apple Account configured for the App Store is required; the purchase command obtains licences for free apps but does not buy paid apps.

It can list available release identifiers and inspect their metadata. Scripts can select a version for download and use JSON output with non-interactive mode to collect results without prompts.

For developers such as mobile developers, automation engineers and security researchers, ipatool is practical for collecting app packages for analysis, automated testing and archiving.

items.title: iptraf-ng
items.author: Curator
items.content:
iptraf-ng is a TUI for observing network traffic and connection statistics and TCP traces and advanced low-level monitoring in the terminal.

The built in traffic monitor separates TCP connections from other packets, showing endpoints, byte counts and TCP flags as traffic arrives. Other views group activity by interface, service port, packet size or LAN station to show how traffic is distributed as it is captured live on the machine.

You can choose which interface to listen on and you can filter or restrict the protocols, addresses and ports shown without changing network rules. The tool logs statistics, and command-line options start a chosen monitor in the background for a timed run. Packet capture requires root access.

For Linux system administrators, network engineers, and security engineers can use iptraf-ng for checking busy connections and identifying which hosts or services account for observed traffic.
